restrictions: The two messages have 55 and 63 bytes: each is one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and its true block length; the 63-byte message ends in eight zero bytes, so that in the zero-filled block of both messages the words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every choice of eight 32-bit words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7, and one of the eight words is the round-1 state word Y4, which the search holds inside a sub-class of 131,072 values, a quarter of the class of 524,288 values of entry c66f230d of the same participant. Heuristic part: a search over 2^101.442 such pairs for one whose remaining 128 digest bits agree. The search works on batches of seven pairs and examines a batch further only if one of its pairs passes a filter on one internal word (rule A, eight bit conditions); rule A is not implied by a collision, and a pair that fails it is examined further only if another pair of its batch passes, and is not counted in the success bound.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; seven trials per 256-bit word in 36-bit lanes on a 16-register load/store machine on which nine words (six masks, three constants of the rule test) stay in registers during a loop over the members and every other memory word costs one load each time it is fetched. Every batch runs stage A, 37 operations plus 10 loads; only a batch in which a trial passes rule A runs stage 2, 105 plus 30. With stage 2 counted for one batch in 32 and with the middle step, the table build and the outer step, a trial is charged 7.7 operations. With a load for every use, the convention of entry c66f230d, the same program counts 57 and 143 and the claim would be 96.0. No sorting or lookup by value and no table that grows with the number of trials: two fixed lists and a table of five lists, 18,725 words each. The algorithm halts with failure when one batch in 32 has run stage 2 or when 2^84 trials that passed the second test have been processed.

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word. The success probability 0.39 holds only under heuristics H1, H2 and H3. The factor 49,400,000 in H1 is assumed and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments; with the uniform rate instead, the same search needs 2^127 trials and gives time_log2 121.3. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed. The loops of the search, their ranges and the processing of a trial that passes the second test are defined in proof.md; the submitted program contains and counts their pieces, not the loops.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta that defines the class, two bits that define the sub-class and three 32-bit constants of the rule test are stored in the program (48 bytes of advice). The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by a participant's count of the solutions of a seven-word system; the sub-class and rule A were proposed by another AI model (GPT Sol 6.1) from exact counts of the same kind, which the participant's counter reproduces. preprocessing_log2 63 bounds only the recomputation of the two pinned message words at the four given inputs; the selection of the constants, the sub-class and the rule is not bounded, and its work is the participant's estimate (below 2^60 operations). memory_log2_bytes 35 covers the memory of that selection as observed by the participant; the search itself needs less than 2^23 bytes. No priority or novelty claim is made. proof.md Section 11 corrects errors in the text of entry c66f230d and Section 13 gives credit.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the 2^101.442 enumerated trials behave, with respect to the event that the 128-bit residual R is zero and the trial satisfies rule A, like independent events of probability at least 49,400,000 * 2^-128 each, to the extent that the probability that no trial has this event is at most exp(-1/2) + 0.002. The assumption has two parts, a rate and the absence of clustering, and neither follows from the other.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 6.4: lengths 55 and 63, the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 in the sub-class of 131,072 values defined by eta = 830303cf and by bits 21 and 26 of e1 (Lemmas Q and Q2), contexts of seven words of which four come from the random word, one (C0.d1) runs over 1,424,469 values and two (w5 and X2) over all 2^32 values, and all members of the sub-class for every context. Rule A is the set of eight bit conditions of Section 6.3 on the word h1 of a trial (Lemma A).
heuristics.extrapolation: From a participant count, in integer arithmetic, of the rate of the sub-class under the seven-word model, that is of the number of solutions with Y4 in the sub-class of the seven-word system that determines R: for each value beta of an auxiliary difference of one of the two calls, every outcome of that call is enumerated, the other call is counted exactly for it, split by rule A, and the probability of the outcome is counted exactly. Over the 60 values of beta that have a part for the whole class the count is 185,377,197.55 times the uniform expectation (53 values and 317 outcomes with a part); 185,358,111.47 of it satisfies rule A; the claim uses 185,355,453.45, the sum over the 99 outcomes in which every solution satisfies rule A. The sub-class and the rule were proposed by another AI model (GPT Sol 6.1) with a counter of its own; its exact fractions for the totals, the rule masses, every value of beta and 3,243 integers on 1,081 outcomes (three per outcome) are equal to the participant's; the recount was made with its figures at hand, and the figure that the claim uses is the participant's alone. From checks of the counter: complete enumeration with 8-bit words including sub-classes and three-bit parities (6,805,032 integers, none different); two functions for the split by the rule that agree on 687 outcomes. From comparisons of the model with real trials at 32 bits in the loop order of this package, for the whole class and other rules: averaged over outer tuples, events of one call down to a probability of about 2^-40 agree with the model (listed E1 outcomes: 138 against 152.0 expected); in the order of entry c66f230d, 24 runs of 2^45 real trials on another machine: 692 against 690.78. From scaled-down end-to-end runs with 8-bit and 10-bit words in this loop order, without sub-class and rule: 470 collisions against 467.6 predicted in 436 runs (the first 92 runs were low, 56 against 74.8, and the later ones were made because of that), and in a larger job of 8,448 runs with expectations written down beforehand 8,108 against 8,313.6 (-2.25 standard deviations: 3.3 percent low with 8-bit words, level with 10-bit words); and in the order of entry c66f230d: 345 against 335.76 in a plan fixed beforehand. All in proof.md Section 10. The factor and the absence of clustering are assumptions; the count is what the factor is set against, not a measurement of the trials, and none of these measurements reaches the joint event (R = 0 and rule A) over the real trials of a run that H1 asks about.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 49,400,000 is assumed. It is set against a participant count of 185,355,453, 3.75 times larger, which the organizer-run experiments do not measure; the success bound needs a factor of at least 49,323,560. With factor 1 (the uniform rate) the claim would be 2^127 trials and time_log2 121.3. The count is exact only under the seven-word model, that six of the seven words behave like independent uniform words over the trials; that the trials of the algorithm meet the counted solutions at the model's rate is the assumption, and so is the absence of clustering, which the model does not address. The model does NOT hold inside one context for rule A (single contexts have between 0.0071 and 0.0421 of their batches entering stage 2 where the average is 0.02617) and NOT inside one outer step for the call E1 (the rate of single events of E1 was seen between 0.02 and 2 times its average from one outer tuple to another); only averages over outer steps have the model's values, and whether the rate of trials that satisfy rule A and have R = 0 has the model's value on average was not measured and cannot be. One count of the layout runs is unexplained (3 events where 14.65 are expected in one window of 2^44 trials). A graphics-card run now measures rule A in the sub-class (24 outer tuples, 2^44.59 real trials; rule A passes at 2^-8.000002 and a marker at 2^-32.2 is about 1.18 times richer in the sub-class than in the whole class, while its deeper marker at 2^-40.15 has 14 counts against 21.59 expected and settles nothing at that precision), and a scaled-down end-to-end run with the sub-class and an eight-condition rule finds collisions at the exact per-trial count (121 against 120.23); but no run reaches rule A together with an event of R, and neither measures the kept mass that H1 is set against (proof.md Section 10). The sub-class and the rule were chosen by the count: the sub-class gains a factor of 1.142 under the model, and no measurement on real messages shows that gain; a choice that is best under the model says nothing about the model. Rule A is not implied by a collision; that it loses only one part in 10,000 of the count inside the sub-class rests on the two counts, and on the whole class it would lose more than half. The count rests on few paths: four values of beta carry 98.8% of it. The list of 60 values of beta rests on uncertified solver answers and on the other model's enumeration. The counting programs are not in the package. All trials of a run share four seed words, the 2^49 trials of an outer step share six words and, for one member, a whole table row, and the 2^52.44 trials of a run with one value of w5 and one member share Y12 and w5; their independence is assumed. The loops, their ranges and the processing of passes are defined in the text and are not in the submitted program. The proofs of the new lemmas (T2, T3, T4, Q2 and Lemma A in its new form) and this whole text were written and checked by helper agents of the participant, instances of one AI model; three further helper agents reviewed the assembled text once, and their corrections and the evidence added after the review were not read again by them; no person has read it. Nothing here is organizer-verified except the two declared experiments, which do not measure the 128-bit rate and are not a test of H1.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than 2^84 of the trials of a run pass the 32-bit E1 test of proof.md Lemma N without having R = 0.
heuristics.scope: The E1 test of Section 6.3 on all trials of Section 6.4, whether or not their batch runs stage 2; the algorithm processes only the passes in batches that run stage 2, which are fewer. A pass rate of 2^-31.41 would give 2^70.03 passes; the budget corresponds to a pass rate of 2^-17.44 and is larger by a factor of more than 2^13.9, and processing 2^84 passes is charged in the time bound (2^94 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: From participant measurements of the pass rate on real trials with these constants at 32 bits in the loop order of this package, for the whole class of 524,288 values of Y4: 2^-31.41 per trial on average and 2^-31.20 in the outer tuple with the most (proof.md Section 10, layout runs), to the trials of one run, which have Y4 in the sub-class.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. For the sub-class the graphics-card run of Section 10 gives 9,537 passes of the E1 test in 2^44.585 trials, a rate of 2^-31.37. It is a mean; that the pass count of a full run, whose outer steps share four seed words, stays near that mean is assumed. The layout runs have random outer words and at most 2^26 values of X2 of one outer tuple. The cost of processing a pass, below 2^10 operations, is stated in words and was not written out on the counting machine. If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H2 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than E of the batches of a run hold a trial that satisfies rule A of proof.md Section 6.3, where E is the budget of Section 6.4, just under one in 32 of the batches; so fewer than E batches run stage 2.
heuristics.scope: Rule A (Lemma A) on the trials of Section 6.4, in the seven-lane batches of Section 6.5. A batch runs stage 2 exactly when one of its seven trials satisfies rule A. The budget E is 18,725 * J / 32 rounded down, with J = 2^110 / 49,400,000 rounded up; a run has at least J pairs of an outer step and a value of X2 and 18,725 batches per pair. The time bound charges stage 2 for that many batches, and the algorithm halts with failure when the budget is reached. The statement is about the total over a run; it is not claimed context by context and is false for single contexts. It holds whenever fewer than E trials of the run satisfy rule A, a share of 1.1429 times 2^-8 of the trials.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the fact that a uniform 32-bit word satisfies the eight conditions of rule A with probability 2^-8, and from participant measurements on real trials of the sub-class at 32 bits on a processor: in 8,192 independent contexts with all members (2^30 trials) the share of the trials that satisfy rule A is 2^-8.0019 and the share of the batches that hold such a trial is 0.02617; in 512 outer steps with 16 values of X2 each, 2^-7.9992 and 0.02622, with the 512 outer steps between 0.0238 and 0.0289; with a second seed, 2^-8.0000 and 0.02622; against the budget 0.03125. For the whole class and the rules with four, five and six conditions, runs on a graphics card in the loop order of this package have the shares of the trials within one part in a million of 2^-4, 2^-5 and 2^-6 on average over outer tuples. All in proof.md Sections 6.5 and 10. The extrapolation is from these averages over sampled contexts to the average over the outer steps of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. The share of the batches of ONE context that run stage 2 is not below the budget in every context: in the samples single contexts have between 0.0071 and 0.0421, and one whole value of X2 that was run in full has 0.0307. Only the average is below it, with room of 19 percent in these samples, which is less room than entry c66f230d had for its budget. That the average over the outer steps of one run, which share four seed words, stays below the budget is assumed; the cause of the dependence on the context is not analysed. Rule A with eight conditions is now recorded on a graphics card for the sub-class as well: of 2^44.59 real trials 103,079,088,429 pass it (2^-8.000002) and 0.026178 of the packed words enter stage 2, confirming the processor shares at 8,192 times the trials (proof.md Section 10). The outer words of these samples are random words; three samples of the review in the ranges of the algorithm give between 0.02617 and 0.02620. If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H3 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005. The operation counts of the two stages are the submitted program's own, on a machine that keeps nine words in registers.
